methods.label: Find the favorable portions of the string
methods.explanation:
Assume that the cut point is uniformly distributed along the string. We may take the string's length to be \(1\), since scaling both pieces does not change their length ratio. Let \(t\), with \(0<t<1\), be the distance of the cut from one end.

The longer piece is always at least as long as the shorter piece. Thus, if \(x\le1\), the required event is certain and its probability is \(1\).

Now suppose \(x>1\). If \(t\le\tfrac12\), the shorter piece has length \(t\), so the condition is
\[
1-t\ge xt
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
t\le\frac{1}{x+1}.
\]
Here \(x+1>0\), and \(1/(x+1)<1/2\), so this describes exactly the favorable cuts in the left half. By the same reasoning, the favorable cuts in the right half satisfy \(t\ge x/(x+1)\). These two portions are disjoint and each has length \(1/(x+1)\). Uniform selection therefore gives
\[
P=\frac{2}{x+1}.
\]
Individual boundary points have probability zero, so including equality or excluding the string's endpoints does not change the result. At \(x=1\), this formula also gives \(1\).

Consequently, choice E is correct when \(x\ge1\). The unstated restriction matters: at \(x=\tfrac12\), the probability is \(1\), while choice E gives \(4/3\). As written, the answer must be given by the piecewise rule above.
